newsitem.title: USA: Ohio airports to receive $13.2 mln federal grants.
newsitem.headline: Ohio airports to receive $13.2 mln federal grants.

text.p: Eleven Ohio airports have been awarded grants totalling $13.2 million for improvements, U.S. Transportation Secretary Rodney Slater announced Tuesday.
* James M. Cox International Airport in Dayton will receive $3.8 million for rescue equipment and taxiway extensions and rehabilitation.
* Port Columbus International Airport in Columbus, $2.9 million for runway extension and relocation of air navigation equipment.
* Hamilton-Fairfield Airport, Hamilton, nearly $1.9 million to rehabilitate a runway and remove obstructions.
* Delaware Municipal Airport, $1.8 million for runway repairs.
* Akron-Canton Regional Airport, Akron, more than $1 million for taxiways, apron, access road, snow removal equipment and drainage improvements.
Grants of less than $1 million also went to airports in Cincinnati, Middletown, Lima, Coshocton and two other Columbus airports.
